Commentary.Commentary: We are back for the chase. The players are out in the middle. Kyle Mayers and Shamarh Brooks are the openers for the Windies. Trent Boult to start with the ball.
...THE CHASE...

Right then, The game is set for the West Indian big-hitters to come and put up a show. This is a high-scoring venue and they will be looking to get the most from this good wicket. New Zealand have their bowling big guns back and will be silently confident that they will be able to defend this target.

Odean Smith is up for a chat. He says apart from the last couple of overs it was good bowling from them. Shares that they had some luck on the field. Informs it is his home ground and he knows the conditions well. On the Hat-trick ball, he says he wanted to go for the yorker but the skipper said no and he then went for a widish delivery. Mentions that this is a high scoring ground and if they set-up properly, and get a good start, they can win.

West Indies bowlers could not get early wickets but they kept working for it. Odean Smith then dismissed the openers in two deliveries and suddenly they seemed to get more control. The break was good as they returned to pick some crucial wickets They would be absolutely thrilled with their catching though. They took quite a few blinders in the field and that was partially the reason for New Zealand not getting out of reach. They will be slightly disappointed with their death bowling as they conceded 34 runs in the last two overs and that took New Zealand to a decent total.

The visitors started well with a 62-run opening partnership. Devon Conway was going well and scored 43 up the order. Once the openers were dismissed in consecutive deliveries, Kane Williamson steadied the innings along with Glenn Phillips. The latter was dismissed right after the break and despite Kane Williamson’s well-made 47, New Zealand could not get ahead of the game as they kept losing wickets. An attacking cameo from James Neesham as he scored 33 of just 15 deliveries, pushed them beyond the 180 mark.

New Zealand will be unsure about the score they have put up here as they have 185 on the board. The pitch looks good to bat on and they would have probably hoped for a bit more. The halt in play seemed to have broken their momentum bit. West Indies will be happy with their bowling effort apart from the last over and will know that they have enough batting to get over the finish line.
FOUR! 23 runs off the last over! 34 off the last two! How costly this could prove to be! Very full and on middle. Neesham sweeps it to deep square leg for a boundary. New Zealand finish with 185/5.

FOUR! make it 19 off the over! Holder not showing his experience and New Zealand are scoring that crucial runs! Fuller ball, outside off. Neesham drives it through point. No chance for Hayden Walsh there for four more.
FOUR! Jason Holder is proving expensive here! This is full and on middle. Neesham whacks it through square leg for a boundary.
DROPPED! A length ball, way outside off. Neesham drags it as he tries to pull and hits it to long on. Romario Shepherd runs to his right and fumbles to complete the catch. Two runs.
A full toss, widish one. Neesham lofts it over cover for a couple of runs. A better throw and there could have been a run out chance.
SIX! POWERED! A length ball, outside off. Neesham stands tall and hammers it over long off for a biggie.
Wide! Serves a length ball, way outside off. Neesham has a wild swing but misses.
Jason Holder comes on to bowl the last over. He has been really good bowling 3 overs for 19 and taking a wicket.
Very full and angling outside off, worked to deep cover for one.
Wide! Slides a full ball down the leg side. Neesham fails to whip it away.
SIX! New Zealand will take it however it comes! On a length and around off. Again Neesham has a big swing across but gets a leading edge and it goes all the way over third man for six.
Beaten again! This one is short and around off, slower again. Neesham fails to pull it.
Length and outside off at 127 clicks. Neesham is beaten as he tries to pull this.
Short of a length and outside off. Santner mistimes his pull to mid on for a single.
On a length and on off. Santner tucks it to deep mid-wicket for a couple.

Serves a widish full delivery. Neesham throws his bat at it but fails to connect. Career best figures for Odean Smith. Did well in the last match against India and follows up with another brilliant figure.
On middle, it is hit to deep square leg for a single.
Length and outside off, punched through covers for a single.
Mitchell Santner walks out to the crease and has some work to do to get New Zealand to a reasonable total.

OUT! TAKEN! Hayden Walsh shows brilliance on the field now! West Indies have been top notch on the field! The fielders are supporting the bowlers really well! Smith gets his third and it is all due to some good fielding he has got wickets. Length and on middle. Kane Williamson heaves across to deep mid-wicket. Hayden Walsh there, runs to his left, dives and takes a superb catch. Covered a good amount of distance.
Commentary.Howout: c Hayden Walsh b Odean Smith

Commentary.Commentary: Brave from Smith! This is short and wide outside off. The third man fielder was in but Smith went for it. Kane Williamson swings and misses.
Wide! Shorter but siding down the leg side Kane Williamson misses his pull.
Around off, drilled down to long on for a single.
Odean Smith has come back for his last over. He has conceded 28 runs in his 3 so far but has taken two crucial wickets.
Fuller ball, slanting on off, Neesham forces it to deep square leg for one more.
Length ball, outside off. Kane Williamson taps it to deep point for a single.
Length ball, outside off. Neesham works it through square leg for a single.
James Neesham makes his way out to the middle and New Zealand will be hoping for another cameo from their player.

OUT! CAUGHT BEHIND! Good comeback from Obed McCoy after getting hit for a six. McCoy angles a slower length ball, across the right-hander. Mitchell swings his bat and tries to go over the leg side but only gets a bottom edge to the keeper. An appeal for caught behind and Daryl Mitchell is given out but he reviews it in the dying seconds. Ultra Edge shows a spike as the ball passes the bat and Mitchell has to walk back. Out it is.
Commentary.Howout: c Devon Thomas b Obed McCoy

Commentary.Commentary: SIX! New Zealand have changed the gears now! On a length and on middle. Daryl Mitchell stays on the back foot and pummels it over long on for six.
QUICK SINGLE! On a length and on off. Kane Williamson guides it to short third man for one.
Length and outside off, steered to third man for a single. 16 off the over. An expensive from Romario Shepherd and Kane Williamson moves to 45 now.
SIX! This is Kane Williamson at his best! Slightly short and on middle. Kane Williamson hangs back and pulls it well over deep square leg for a biggie.
Slower in pace, length and outside off. Kane Williamson swings and misses.
FOUR! Didn't time it well but still bags a boundary! A full toss on middle. Kane Williamson chips it over the bowler but it was hit right in between the long on and long off fielder.
FOUR! Well played! Too full and around middle. Kane Williamson gets low and whacks it to deep square leg for a boundary.
Fuller ball, outside off, punched through covers for a single.

SIX! A good way to end the over! This is full and way outside off. Kane Williamson has the width to free his arms and smash it over long off for a biggie. Kane Williamson looks to be getting into an higher gear now.
This is bowled a fraction short and outside off, Daryl Mitchell gets across and pulls the ball to deep sqaure leg. They look for two but have to settle for a single.

Deceived by the slower delivery once again. Odean Smith serves this full and outside off, Kane Williamson is early into his shot and gets an inside edge onto his pads. the ball rolls towards cover and they take a single.
Wide! Odean Smith bowls a slower yorker but strays down the leg stump. Kane Williamson looks to flick but misses. This is called wide by the umpire.
Odean Smith bowls a slower delivery on a good length and outside off, Kane Williamson mistimes the ball towards cover.
This is bowled on a good length and follows the batter to the leg side, Daryl Mitchell clips this to short fine leg and takes a single.

Odean Smith serves this full on middle and leg, Daryl Mitchell clips this towards the deep square leg fence. Shimron Hetmyer does not read the spin at the boundary but just about manages to stop it. They take two runs.

That would have been another blinder! Jason Holder bangs in a slower bouncer and Kane Williamson goes for the pull. Does not get good timing and the ball just goes above the head of short fine leg. Kyle Mayers stretches his arm over his head and gets his hand to it. However, he can not hold on and they take a couple of runs.
Jason Holder bowls an off-cutter full and outside off, Kane Williamson goes for the shot and gets beaten on the inside edge as the ball nips back in.
This is a full toss outside off, Daryl Mitchell knocks this to the right of mid off and takes a single.
Serves this on a good length and just outside off, Kane Williamson punches this to the right of the diving bowler and takes a run as the ball goes to long on.
Jason Holder goes full and in line with the stumps, Daryl Mitchell works this towards long on and takes a single.
Back-of-a-length delivery wide outside off, Daryl Mitchell taps this towards short fine leg.
Bowls this one quicker and fires it full into the stumps, Daryl Mitchell works this towards deep mid-wicket for a single. Six singles in the over and a good one from Hayden Walsh.
This is a fraction short and outside off, Kane Williamson plays this toward backward point and takes a single. There is a half stop and some undecisive running.
Hayden Walsh continues bowling it full outside off, Daryl Mitchell paddles this towards fine leg for another single.
Goes full once again and angles it into the pads, Kane Williamson works this towards deep mid-wicket for a single.
That is 100 for New Zealand. This is a loopy delivery bowled full outside off, Daryl Mitchell gets down the wicket and punches it tow long off for a run.
Hayden Walsh flights this full outside off, Kane Williamson knocks the ball to long off for a single.
Daryl Mitchell is the new man in.

OUT! CAUGHT! Perfect start for West Indies after the rain interval! Jason Holder bangs this  one in short and angles the ball into the batter. Glenn Phillips goes for the pull and gets the ball high on his bat. It lobs up into the air and goes towards short fine leg. Kyle Mayers has an easy catch and Glenn Phillips has to depart. New Zealand have lost their third.
Commentary.Howout: c Kyle Mayers b Jason Holder

Commentary.Commentary: Jason Holder bowls a slower delivery full and just outside off, Kane Williamson works this wide of long on and takes another run.
Goes a fraction full and angles the ball into the pads, Glenn Phillips clips this to the left of short fine leg and takes a run.
Jason Holder begins with a good length delivery outside off, Kane Williamson guides it to third man for a single.
Resumption! A quick mop up is going on as the players take their position. The good thing is no overs are lost. Jason Holder will finish his over.

Update - 2.25 am IST (8.55 pm GMT, previous day) - Finally some really good news! We are going to have some cricket. The umpires are through with their inspection. The game is set to restart at 2.40 am IST (9.10 pm GMT, previous day). Also, no overs lost.

Update - 2.00 am IST (8.30 pm GMT, previous day) - The sun is out and the covers are off! The groundstaff is working hard to dry up the outfield. There will be an inspection at 2.15 am IST (8.45 pm GMT, previous day). We should have some action shortly.

Update - 1.45 am IST (8.15 pm GMT, previous day) - Some good news folks! The rain seems to have subsided and the groundstaff has made their way out to the middle. They will begin mopping up the water and hopefully, the covers will be off to allow play to resume soon. Stay tuned for further updates and the inspection time.

Update - 1.09 am IST (7.39 pm GMT, previous day) - Still no positive updates. In fact, the rain seems to have gotten heavier. The weather has changed all of a sudden and the sky looks really gloomy now. The good news is that 90 minutes can be added to play and there are lights as well that can be used if it gets dark. Stay tuned for further updates.

Update - 12.53 am IST (7.23 pm GMT, previous day) - Play halted! It has started to rain. Thankfully, it is just drizzling but the umpire does not want to waste time and asks the players to walk off. The covers are on. Hopefully, it is just a passing shower and we resume quickly. Stay tuned.
This is slightly back of a length and in line with the stumps, Kane Williamson nudges this towards mid-wicket.

FOUR! Kane Williamson is looking good. Jason Holder bowls this short and wide outside off, Kane Williamson comes down the wicket but has enough room to cut this towards deep point. Kyle Mayers puts in a dive at the boundary but can not stop the ball. That is four more runs for Kane Williamson.
Jason Holder is back on.

Hayden Walsh continues bowling short and wide outside off, Kane Williamson stays back and cuts this late towards deep backward point. A good stop from Obed McCoy at the boundary line but the batters are able to take three runs.
Short once again and outside off, Kane Williamson works this towards short third man but does not take a single this time.
WIDE! Flights this full and outside off. This is far from the batter and he leaves it alone. The umpire calls that wide.
This is short and on the pads, Glenn Phillips gets an inside edge to deep square leg as he looks to pull this.
Flights this and bowls it slower in the air. This is full and outside off, Kane Williamson guides it to short third man for a quick single.
Hayden Walsh goes 'round the wicket and fires this one short and outside off, Glenn Phillips slaps this towards deep cover and takes a single.

SIX! BANG! What a start after the break! Hayden Walsh flights this one full and outside off, Glenn Phillips gets a hold of this one and thumps it straight back over the bowler's head for a maximum! This was huge!

Drinks - New Zealand started in a steady manner and got off to a good start. The openers were looking good and the platform was being set for the hitters to take over. However, both of them departed in consecutive deliveries and allowed the West Indians to claw back into the game. A lot of work for both sides to do after the break.
A dot to end the over! This is on middle, it is hit to mid-wicket.
Fuller ball and on middle. Kane Williamson bunts it to mid-wicket.
On middle, on a length, nudged to mid-wicket for a single.
Odean Smith is doing well to hit the deck hard and use the surface. This is outside off. Phillips looks to cut at it but misses.
FOUR! Short and outside off. Phillips waits on the back foot and upper cuts it over backward point for a boundary.
Length ball, tailing on the pads, whipped behind square on the leg side for a single.
Tossed up, way outside off, worked to deep cover for a single.
A leg-breaker, flatter and outside off. Kane Williamson uses his feet and reaches to the pitch of the ball to block it.
A leggie, full and outside off. Phillips drives it to deep cover for one.
Floated ball, around off, pushed to long off for one.
Flatter, quicker and outside off. Kane Williamson cuts it straight to point.
On middle, pushed to covers for a single.

FOUR! Great placement from Kane Williamson!  Odean Smith continues bowling short and wide outside off. Kane Williamson gets on his toes and on top of the bounce to work this past the backward point fielder for a boundary. Two wickets and two boundaries in the over.
Odean Smith goes short once again and wide outside off, Glenn Phillips slaps this towards deep point and gets off the mark with a single.
WIDE! Serves this way outside off from a shorter length. Called wide by the umpire. The hat-trick ball is wasted.
Glenn Phillips has made his way out to the crease to face the Hat-trick delivery!

OUT! CAUGHT BEHIND! Devon Thomas with acrobatic stuff now! West Indies with some brilliance on the field! Smith bowls a slower length ball on middle. Conway looks to pull but gets deceived by the pace of the ball and gets a leading edge. Now, Devon Thomas, the keeper was trying to run on the leg side but had to readjusts quickly as the ball lobed towards him and to his left. He shuffles to that side, dives, and the ball sticks in his left-glove. Odean Smith is on a Hat trick.
Commentary.Howout: c Devon Thomas b Odean Smith

Commentary.Commentary: The skipper, Kane Williamson makes his way out to the middle.

OUT! CAUGHT! Outstanding from Hetmyer! Acrobatic stuff in the deep from Shimron Hetmyer! What a catch this is! Smith hits the hard length and serves it outside off. Martin Guptill swings his bat and toe ends his shot to deep point. Shimron Hetmyer there was standing inches away from the ropes but he judged his jump to perfection, jumped and took a one handed-stunner to dismiss Guptill. The ball stuck nicely to his left-hand.
Commentary.Howout: c Shimron Hetmyer b Odean Smith

Commentary.Commentary: Short again but this time on middle. Guptill tries to ramp it over but misses.
FOUR! Boundary to start the over then! Smith serves a short ball, outside off. Guptill slashes to it, gets a top edge but the ball flies to the vacant third man region for four runs.
Odean Smith has been given the ball now. West Indies will be hoping he gets a breakthrough.
A huge appeal for LBW but not given! Tossed up, full and around leg. Conway tries to reverse sweep it but misses and gets hit on the forearm. it was pitching outside leg.
Shorter, quicker and around leg. Conway tucks it to square leg.
FOUR! Poor delivery! this is full and down the leg side. Conway needs to just get some bat on it and he gets as he tries to sweep this. He gets an inside edge to the fine leg fence.
On a length and on middle. Conway skips down and keeps it out.
Flatter ball, outside off, cut to deep point for a single.
Starts with a fuller ball on the pads, flicked to mid-wicket for a single.
Hayden Walsh has been brought into the attack now that the Powerplay has ended.
A single to end the over! 14 runs off the over. On off, pushed to mid off for a single. At the end of the Powerplay, New Zealand are 52/0 with Devon Conway hitting the bulk of runs.
SIX! Fifty up for the Kiwis! Bright start for them! This is short and on leg. Conway looks to pull but gets a top edge and it flies all the way over fine leg for a biggie.
Two again! This is good running! On a length and outside off. Conway punches it to deep cover. A little bit of fumble and it gives a chance for the second run.
Angles a full ball, wide of off. Conway looks to drive but gets a thick outside edge to deep backward point for another couple of runs.
This is on the pads. Conway flicks it square on the leg side for a couple of runs.
On a length and on off. Guptill whips it to deep square leg for a single.
Short ball bowled slow and outside off, Devon Conway goes for the pull and gets beaten by the pace.
Good-length delivery outside off, Devon Conway guides this towards this backward point fielder.
Obed McCoy serves this full and outside off, Martin Guptill hits this towards mid off and takes a quick single.
Obed McCoy goes back to bowling on a good length and takes some pace off the ball. Martin Guptill goes for a similar shot and misses this time.

SIX! Martin Guptill finally gets a shot away! Obed McCoy bowls this a fraction full and outside off, Martin Guptill takes his front foot forward and lofts the ball handsomely over the deep mid-wicket fence for a maximum. This should get Martin Guptill going.
Obed McCoy bowls this on a good length and outside off, Devon Conway charges down the wicket and strokes the ball to mid off. They take a single as the ball is not picked up cleanly by the fielder.
Romario Shepherd bowls a slower delivery full and outside off, Martin Guptill swings across the line and misses once again.
Romario Shepherd goes full and outside off, Martin Guptill is not connecting well as he mistimes his shot towards cover.
This is short and wide outside off, Devon Conway slaps this towards deep point and takes a single.

FOUR! That is a smart short! Romario Shepherd continues bowling on a good length and this a fraction outside off, Devon Conway moves across the stumps and paddles the ball really fine. Goes to the right of the keeper and runs away to the fine leg fence.
Beaten! This is bowled on a good length and shaping away outside off, Devon Conway pushes at it and gets beaten on the outside edge.
Romario Shepherd begins with a full delivery outside off, Devon Conway strokes this straight to cover.
Romario Shepherd is into the attack.
Obed McCoy serves this on a good length once again, and just outside off, Martin Guptill charges down the wicket and swings. Gets no connection as it goes through to the keeper.
Obed McCoy goes slightly short and outside off, Devon Conway slashes at this towards backward point. Hayden Walsh dives to his left and stops well to restrict the batters to just a single.
This is angling into the pads from a good length, Devon Conway flicks this towards deep backward square leg for a brace.

FOUR! A lucky boundary for Devon Conway but they all count! Obed McCoy bowls this on a good length and outside off, Devon Conway pushes at the ball and gets an inside edge that flies past the stumps towards the fine leg fence for four runs.
On a good length and in line with the stumps, Martin Guptill clips this towards deep square leg for a single.
The is full as well and just outside off, Martin Guptill hits this hard towards the cover fielder.
WIDE! Goes wide outside off this time on a fuller length. The umpire raises his arms to call wide once again.
Obed McCoy begins with a loosener angling down leg stump from a good length. Martin Guptill leaves this alone and the umpire indicates it is wide..

FOUR! Another good over ends with a boundary! Jason Holder goes full and right under the bat outside off, Devon Conway strokes this elegantly through covers for a boundary. The ball races away to the deep cover fence for four more runs.
Jason Holder goes for the yorker and wide outside off, Devon Conway tries to get bat on it and misses. Goes through to the keeper.
Jason Holder serves a full toss outside off, Devon Conway is down the wicket and has to adjust his shot as he guides it towards deep backward point for a brace.
Goes a fraction full and outside off, Devon Conway knocks this straight to cover.
On a good length once again and just outside off, Devon Conway fends this into pitch, and the ball rolls towards the keeper.
Jason Holder starts with a good-length delivery but angling into the pads. Martin Guptill clips this towards deep backward square leg for a single.

SIX! That has gone all the way! Kyle Mayers continues bowling full and wide outside off, Devon Conway gets a stride forward and hits through the line. Gets the ball well over the deep cover fence for a biggie. That is the first boundary for New Zealand.
Jason Holder to start from the other end.
WIDE! Bowls this full and really wide outside off. Devon Conway leaves this alone and is called wide by the umpire.
Devon Conway showing some aggression. Kyle Mayers serves this on a good length and outside off. Devon Conway charges down the wicket and slaps it to mid off.
A fraction full and angling away from the left-hander. Devon Conway fends this back to the bowler.
Goes full once again outside off, Martin Guptill shuffles forward and goes for the booming drive. Gets an inside edge to fine leg for a single.
This is on a good length and angling into the stumps, Martin Guptill flicks this towards square leg.
Kyle Mayers begins with a full delivery pitching outside off, Martin Guptill strokes this straight to mid off.

We are all set for the action. The players are out in the middle. The Windies players take the knee to support the 'BLM' movement. Martin Guptill and Devon Conway are the openers for New Zealand. Kyle Mayers to start with the ball. Here we go...

Phil Simmons is up for a chat. He says they need to recognize how they want to play. Adds that there is a lot of pressure on Nicholas Pooran after the India series but he is learning quickly. Shares that they are working on how to play the middle phase and there will be bounce here so they hope to do better. Admits the pace bowlers need to play with pressure. It was hard against India but they need to do better against the Kiwis.
PITCH REPORT - Daren Ganga is pitchside. He says it is dry and hard. Not a lot of green grass and expect there to bounce. The average score here is 134. Expects an even contest between bat and ball.

Kane Williamson, the skipper of New Zealand. He says it is important to get balance and break as all the players are in different stages of their life. It was nice to be at home and get some break. Informs there are few changes from the game they had against Netherlands.

Nicholas Pooran, the captain of West Indies. He says they will bowl first as the conditions are new for them. Says it is different from Miami and the conditions suit the seamers more so they want to capitalize on that by bowling first. Says that they have been playing a lot of cricket and some of the guys are rested. Continues to say that they have a lot of reserve players and they can put together a good composition and guys are eager to take the opportunity. Says that the team spoke about building partnerships, winning crucial moments and says most importantly it is an opportunity for the young players to gain knowledge and experience. About the team he says that there is one spinner and he can not recall the whole team.

New Zealand (Playing XI) - Martin Guptill, Devon Conway (WK), Kane Williamson (C), Glenn Phillips, Daryl Mitchell, James Neesham, Mitchell Santner, Ish Sodhi, Tim Southee, Lockie Ferguson, Trent Boult.
West Indies (Playing XI) - Kyle Mayers, Shamarh Brooks, Devon Thomas (WK), Nicholas Pooran (C), Shimron Hetmyer, Rovman Powell, Jason Holder, Odean Smith, Romario Shepherd, Obed McCoy, Hayden Walsh.
TOSS - West Indies have won the toss and will BOWL first!

West Indies, on the other hand, find themselves racing against the clock to get their team in place and to get all their players back in form. They have shown glimpses of talent and ability, but they lack consistency. They have match-winners throughout their lineup, yet there are days when all of them fail to click. However, if that switch were to come on, this young West Indian side could prove to be devastating in the World Cup. The team banks heavily on their all-rounders and they bat deep. It will be interesting to see how they face up to their newest opponents, after their recent series defeat to India. They favor this format and if a renaissance of West Indian cricket is to be seen, it will most likely start from T20 cricket. It is hot in Sabina Park despite being cloudy and there is always a chance of rain. The only rain we really want to see though is when it is raining boundaries. Stay tuned as we bring you the toss and other updates…
